hindi: शक्ति की अपेक्षा रखने वाला विजिगीषु षाड्गुण्य का प्रयोग करे।
english: The conqueror, having regard to power, should employ the sixfold policy.
notes: Compound śakti-apekṣa read as a bahuvrīhi (having regard to power); śakti = power per the glossary (the three powers are not named here).

hindi: सम और श्रेष्ठ के साथ सन्धि करे, हीन के साथ विग्रह करे।
english: [One] should make a treaty with an equal and a superior; [one] should make war with an inferior.
notes: sandhīyeta has passive-looking form but is read as middle 'should make a treaty'; alternative 'a treaty should be made'. vigraha rendered 'war' (विग्रह kept in Hindi); the glossary has no Book 7 line for vigraha. jyāyas = superior (in strength); hīna = inferior.

hindi: क्योंकि श्रेष्ठ द्वारा विगृहीत, मानो हाथी के साथ पैदल-युद्ध में पहुँचता है।
english: For, made war upon by a superior, [one] goes, as it were, to a foot-fight with an elephant.
notes: Subject unexpressed (the one made war upon). abhyupaiti 'goes up to, approaches'; pāda-yuddha 'fight on foot'.

hindi: और समान के साथ, कच्चे से टकराए हुए कच्चे बर्तन की तरह, दोनों ओर क्षय करता है।
english: And with an equal, like an unbaked vessel struck by an unbaked [one], [it] brings about loss on both sides.

text_flags.why: possible: ahata 'unstruck' gives no sense here; āhata 'struck' (āmenāhatam) expected

notes: Subject of karoti not expressed (war with an equal, continuing from the previous unit). pātra read as 'vessel' (pot).

hindi: घड़े के साथ पत्थर की तरह, हीन के साथ एकतरफ़ा सिद्धि पाता है।
english: Like a stone with a pot, [one] obtains one-sided success with an inferior.
notes: eka-anta-siddhi taken as 'success on one side only'; alternative 'certain/exclusive success'. Subject unexpressed.

words.gloss: conduct of one submitting with his army

hindi: यदि श्रेष्ठ सन्धि की इच्छा न करे, सेना सहित समर्पण करने वाले के आचरण या आबलीयस योग को अपनाए।
english: If the superior does not wish for a treaty, [one] should adopt the conduct of one submitting with his army, or the ābalīyasa yoga.
notes: daṇḍa = army (glossary 12.1: daṇḍa-upanata = one submitting with his army). ābalīyasa is kept untranslated; yoga left as yoga (sense unsettled in Book 7: course/means). Subject of ātiṣṭhet is the inferior, unexpressed.

hindi: यदि सम सन्धि की इच्छा न करे, जितना अपकार करे, उतना इसके प्रति बदले में अपकार करे।
english: If an equal does not wish for a treaty, as much as he would harm, that much [one] should harm him in return.
notes: asya is a genitive ('his'); read as dative-like 'to him'. Subject of apakuryāt is the equal.

hindi: क्योंकि तेज जोड़ने का कारण है।
english: For spirit [is] the cause of joining.
notes: tejas = spirit (also 'heat, fire, energy'); sandhāna = joining, uniting, as the next unit shows with iron (not 'treaty' as such).

hindi: बिना तपाया हुआ लोहा लोहे के साथ नहीं जुड़ता।
english: Unheated iron does not join with iron.
notes: The closing iti follows a statement with no opening quotation and is not rendered (glossary 3.20). sandhatta = sandhatte before iti.

hindi: यदि हीन सर्वत्र विनीत रहे, सन्धि स्वीकार करे।
english: If the inferior should remain submissive everywhere, [one] should accept a treaty.
notes: The subject of upeyāt is unexpressed: the superior (accepting the inferior's submission) is the likely reading; the inferior himself is not excluded. anupraṇata 'bowed in conformity'.

hindi: क्योंकि वन की अग्नि की तरह दुःख और अमर्ष से उत्पन्न तेज को आगे बढ़ाता है।
english: For, like a forest fire, [he] makes the spirit born of distress and indignation advance.
notes: Subject unexpressed (the inferior). vikramayati (causative of vi-√kram) rendered literally; alternatives 'sets in action' or 'makes display prowess'. amarṣa = indignation (intolerance of wrong).

hindi: और मण्डल के द्वारा अनुग्रह किए जाने योग्य होता है।
english: And [he] becomes one to be favoured by the circle.
notes: Subject unexpressed. maṇḍalasya is a genitive; 'by the circle' (of kings) is the sense taken, alternative 'one to be favoured of the circle'.

hindi: यदि संहित हो, “दूसरे की प्रकृतियाँ, लोभी, क्षीण, अनुचित आचरण पाई हुई या पुनः ग्रहण के भय से नहीं आतीं” देखे, हीन भी विग्रह करे।
english: If [he is] allied and should see: “The other's constituent elements, [being] greedy, impoverished, ill-treated, or from fear of retaking, do not come over”, even [if] inferior [he] should make war.

text_flags.suggest: paśyet (sandhi paśyed dhīno) or paśyed hīno
text_flags.why: possible typo: doubled d and a space before hīno; the e-text spells t+h as 'dd h'

notes: saṃhita 'allied, joined (in treaty)'; the object of upagacchanti is unexpressed (the enemy king is the likely goal: the enemy's elements do not go over to him). The pratyādāna 'retaking' is kept literal. The quotation opens and closes within this unit. kṣīṇa 'impoverished', alternative 'diminished'.

hindi: यदि विगृहीत हो, “दूसरे की प्रकृतियाँ, लोभी, क्षीण, अनुचित आचरण पाई हुई या विग्रह से उद्विग्न, मेरे पास नहीं आतीं” देखे, श्रेष्ठ भी सन्धि करे, या विग्रह से उत्पन्न उद्वेग को शान्त करे।
english: If made war upon and [he] should see: “The other's constituent elements, [being] greedy, impoverished, ill-treated, or distressed by war, do not come to me”, even [if] superior [he] should make a treaty, or should allay the distress from war.
notes: Quotation opens and closes within the unit. Subject of the main clause is the one made war upon (unexpressed). Compare unit 13.

hindi: विपत्तियों के एक साथ होने पर भी, “मैं भारी व्यसन वाला हूँ, हल्के व्यसन वाला दूसरा सरलता से अपने व्यसन का प्रतीकार करके आक्रमण कर सकता है” देखे, श्रेष्ठ भी सन्धि करे।
english: Even in the simultaneity of calamities, [if] [he] should see: “I am one with a heavy calamity; the other, with a light calamity, having easily remedied his own calamity, might attack”, even [if] superior [he] should make a treaty.
notes: No cet in the Sanskrit: the conditional is only implied, shown in brackets in English. Hindi has no यदि. ātmanaḥ 'of himself, his own'. vyasana here = calamity (of a king at war), glossary 8.1.

hindi: यदि सन्धि और विग्रह में दूसरे का क्षीण होना या अपनी वृद्धि न देखे, श्रेष्ठ भी चुप बैठा रहे।
english: If in treaty and war [one] does not see weakening of the other or increase of himself, even [if] superior [he] should stay quiet.
notes: āsīta literally 'should sit'; rendered 'stay quiet' after the glossary (āsana = staying quiet). Subject unexpressed. ātman 'self' rendered 'himself'.

hindi: यदि दूसरे के व्यसन को अप्रतिकार्य देखे, हीन भी चढ़ाई करे।
english: If [one] should see the calamity of the other [to be] irremediable, even [if] inferior [he] should march against [him].

text_flags.suggest: paśyet (sandhi paśyed dhīno) or paśyed hīno
text_flags.why: possible typo: doubled d and a space before hīno; same spelling as in unit 13

notes: Subject and object of abhiyāyāt unexpressed; 'against [him]' is bracketed.

hindi: या श्रेष्ठ भी, जिसका व्यसन अप्रतिकार्य, निकट है, आश्रय ले।
english: Or even a superior, [one] whose calamity [is] irremediable [and] imminent, should seek shelter.
notes: Sanskrit has no object for saṃśrayeta (shelter with another is understood). āsanna = near, imminent; the three members read as two adjectives on vyasana, with no ca.

hindi: यदि एक ओर सन्धि से, एक ओर विग्रह से कार्य की सिद्धि देखे, श्रेष्ठ भी द्वैधीभूत रहे।
english: If [one] should see success of the task by treaty on one side [and] by war on the other, even [if] superior [he] should remain twofold.
notes: dvaidhī-bhūta 'become twofold' is the participial form of the dual policy (dvaidhī-bhāva, glossary 8.5).

hindi: इस प्रकार सम का षाड्गुण्य का उपयोग है।
english: In this way [is] the employment of the sixfold policy by an equal.
notes: samasya taken as 'of the equal' (sama); the construction is elliptical and the reading is not certain (the previous units cover superior, equal and inferior together).

hindi: किन्तु उसमें विशेष भेद है।
english: But there [is] a particular distinction.
notes: tatra 'there, in that (matter)'; prativiśeṣa 'particular distinction' (alternative 'detailed specification').

words.gloss: whose wheel is set in motion

hindi: जिसका चक्र प्रवृत्त है, ऐसे बलवान राजा से आक्रान्त निर्बल सन्धि द्वारा शीघ्र कोश, सेना, स्वयं, भूमि के साथ समर्पण करे।
english: The weak, overrun by a strong king whose wheel is set in motion, should quickly submit by a treaty, with treasury, army, self and land.
notes: pravṛtta-cakra taken literally ('whose wheel is set in motion'); the sense (sovereignty or army on the move) is not fixed. daṇḍa = army (glossary, prakṛti sense). The instrumental of the four items is read as 'with' (the means of the submission); ātma = self (himself).

hindi: “स्वयं गिनी हुई सेना के साथ, या सेना के वैभव के साथ उपस्थित होना चाहिए” यह सन्धि आत्म-आमिष मानी गई है।
english: “[One] must attend [him] oneself, with a counted army or with the resources of the army”: this treaty is considered the ātma-āmiṣa [treaty].
notes: upasthātavyam is impersonal, so 'oneself' and the object [him] are supplied in brackets. vibhava taken as 'resources' (alternatives: might, wealth); daṇḍasya vibhavena could also be 'with the might of the army'. ātma-āmiṣa kept as a name; āmiṣa literally 'flesh, bait, prize'. daṇḍa = army.

words.gloss: commander of the army and prince

hindi: “सेनापति और कुमार को उपस्थित होना चाहिए”, यह पुरुषान्तर सन्धि हो सकती है; “स्वयं नहीं”; आत्म-रक्षण वाली।
english: “The commander of the army and the prince must attend [him]”: this may be the puruṣa-antara treaty (treaty through another man); “not by himself”: [it is] self-protecting.
notes: puruṣa-antara = another man (cf. puruṣa-sandhi, glossary 12.1).

words.gloss: protecting the chiefs of the army and himself

hindi: “एक के द्वारा दूसरी जगह जाना चाहिए, स्वयं या सेना के साथ” यह अदृष्ट-पुरुष सन्धि है, सेना के मुखियों और स्वयं की रक्षा करने वाली।
english: “[It] is to be marched elsewhere by one, himself or with the army”: this treaty, adṛṣṭa-puruṣa (having an unseen man), [is] protecting the chiefs of the army and himself.
notes: ekena is unclear (one person, or one of the two); kept literal. The first line is a quoted condition closed by iti; ayam begins the predicate. daṇḍa-mukhya = chiefs of the army (glossary 9.7). adṛṣṭa-puruṣa kept as a name with its literal sense in the gloss.

words.gloss: treaties of submitting with the army

hindi: पहले दो में मुख्यों और स्त्रियों का बन्धन करे, किन्तु अन्तिम में शत्रु को गूढ़ रूप से साधे। ये सेना सहित समर्पण की सन्धियाँ हैं।
english: In the first two [one] should do the binding of chiefs and women, but in the last [one] should secretly accomplish the enemy. Such [are] these treaties of submitting with the army.
notes: mukhya-strī could also be 'the chiefs' women' or 'chief women'. sādhayet with a person as object: win over or dispatch; left as 'accomplish'. pūrvayoḥ/paścime refer to the three treaties of units 23-25. Closing 'ity ete ...' follows the glossary (Such [are]).

hindi: कोश देने से शेष प्रकृतियों का छुड़ाना परिक्रय सन्धि हो; और वही यथासुख।
english: The release of the remaining constituent elements by the giving of the treasury would be the parikraya treaty (ransom), and that very [one] [is] according to ease.
notes: The last clause is elliptical (no verb); yathā-sukham 'according to ease/as one pleases' is obscure here and kept literal. parikraya 'ransom, buying off'.

words.gloss: to be brought by the skandha

hindi: स्कन्ध द्वारा लाए जाने योग्य सन्धि उपग्रह अनेक प्रकार से जानी जानी चाहिए; देश और काल से निरुद्ध उपग्रह अत्यय हो।
english: The treaty to be brought by the skandha [is] to be known in many ways, [as] upagraha; the upagraha restrained by place and time would be atyaya.
notes: Obscure: skandha (shoulder, mass, contingent), upagraha (seizure, support, provision) and atyaya (lapse, penalty) are kept untranslated or literal; a person should check against the edition's commentary. The structure is uncertain.

hindi: सहने योग्य के दान से भविष्य में समर्थ, स्त्री-बन्धन से भी; सुवर्ण सन्धि विश्वास से एकीभाव को प्राप्त हुई हो।
english: Capable in the future from giving what is bearable, even from binding of women: the suvarṇa treaty (gold treaty) would be one gone to oneness through trust.
notes: Obscure syntax; the first line has no clear subject. suvarṇa kept as a name with 'gold' in the gloss. kṣama 'capable/enduring' (alternative 'able to bear').

hindi: विपरीत कपाल होगा, अत्यादान से कहा गया; पहले दो में कुप्य, या गर से युक्त हाथी-घोड़े आगे लाए।
english: The opposite would be the kapāla, spoken of with excessive taking; in the first two [one] should bring forward raw materials, or elephants and horses accompanied by gara.
notes: kapāla kept as a name. atyādāna-abhibhāṣita is obscure (alternatively 'addressed by excessive demand'). gara-anvita may qualify only the elephants and horses or both items. pūrvayoḥ refers to the first two treaties of the kośa-upanata group.

words.gloss: treaties of submitting with the treasury

hindi: तीसरे में कर्मों के क्षय को कहता हुआ धन आगे लाए, चौथे में रहे। ये कोश सहित समर्पण की सन्धियाँ हैं।
english: In the third [one] should bring forward wealth, stating the loss of the works; in the fourth [one] should remain. Such [are] these treaties of submitting with the treasury.
notes: karma rendered 'works' (undertakings; 'actions' also possible). artha = wealth. Closing 'ity ete ...' follows the glossary.

words.gloss: by abandoning one part of the land
protection of the remaining constituent elements

hindi: भूमि के एक भाग के त्याग से शेष प्रकृतियों की रक्षा; वहाँ आदिष्ट सन्धि गूढ़ चोरों को क्षति पहुँचाने वाले के लिए अभीष्ट है।
english: Protection of the remaining constituent elements by abandoning one part of the land: the ādiṣṭa treaty is approved there, for one injuring secret thieves.
notes: gūḍha-stena-upaghātin is obscure: 'injuring secret thieves', or 'secretly injuring thieves' (gūḍha as adverb), or 'secret agents and thieves'. The genitive is read as 'for' (of the one). ādiṣṭa kept as a name (literally 'assigned').

words.gloss: of one awaiting the calamity of the other

hindi: जिन भूमियों के सार ले लिए गए हैं, उनका मूल को छोड़कर झुकाना; वहाँ उच्छिन्न सन्धि दूसरे के व्यसन की प्रतीक्षा करने वाले के लिए अभीष्ट है।
english: The causing to bow of the lands whose valuables are taken, excepting the base: the ucchinna treaty is approved there, for one awaiting the calamity of the other.
notes: praṇāmana (causing to bow, bringing under) is kept literal. ucchinna kept as a name (literally 'cut off'). kāṅkṣin 'desiring, awaiting' (glossary: ākāṅkṣ = await).

hindi: फल देने से भूमियों का छुड़ाना अवक्रय होगा; भूमियों से फल से अतिमुक्त सन्धि वह परिदूषण है।
english: The release of the lands by the giving of fruit would be avakraya (hire); the treaty released beyond fruit from the lands, that [is] the paridūṣaṇa.
notes: avakraya = hire after the glossary (4.1, 5.2); 'buying back, redemption' is the other possible sense here and may fit better. phala-atimukta is obscure (atimukta 'released, given up' beyond/with fruit). paridūṣaṇa kept as a name.

words.gloss: treaties of submitting with a region

hindi: अवेक्षण करे पहले दो में; किन्तु अन्तिम दो में आबलीयस; फल लेकर। ये प्रदेश सहित समर्पण की सन्धियाँ हैं।
english: [One] should exercise regard for the first two, but ābalīyasa for the last two, having taken fruit. Such [are] these treaties of submitting with a region.
notes: Syntax uncertain: pūrvau and paścimau are nominative/accusative dual and kuryāt is singular; the object of avekṣaṇam is unclear (first two kinds), the last two take ābalīyasa. ābalīyasa untranslated as in unit 6. deśa = region (glossary 3.16).

hindi: अपने कार्यों के वश से ये देश और काल में कहे गए हैं; आबलीयसिक तीन प्रकार की हीन-सन्धियाँ करनी चाहिए।
english: By the sway of one's own tasks these have been spoken of in place and in time; the ābalīyasika, three kinds of treaties of the inferior, are to be made.
notes: vaśena 'by the sway/control of'. The syntax of the second line (ābalīyasika as adjective or a name; treaties of the inferior of three kinds) is uncertain; ābalīyasika left untranslated.
